title: Prelaunch staged eviction and rollforward playbook
summary: Working session to finalize staged eviction strategy for KV/prefix cache, rollforward vs rollback decision tree, and handoff/runbook ownership ahead of next-week launch window. Focus on minimizing regen latencies and clear oncall steps.
action_items: Miguel Torres | Draft staged-eviction runbook with thresholds and comms template | 2026-08-25
Lena Sfren | Add eviction metrics to dashboard + alert thresholds | 2026-08-22
Connor Blake | Run two canary simulations with traffic shape A/B and report lat/p99/cost | 2026-08-24
Elena Park | Schedule launch-room rehearsal and invite stakeholders | 2026-08-20

Schedule canary on staging clusters next Tue/Wed

transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-08-19 09:00 PDT
Duration: 75m
Attendees: Ava, Miguel, Jordan, Lena, Ravi, Maya, Connor, Elena
Agenda: staged eviction policy, rollforward decision tree, canary plan, runbook ownership

[00:00] Ava: ok thanks everyone for carving time. let's run through the staged eviction plan. we're aiming to avoid mass regen when a model switch or traffic burst happens. Miguel can you start with the summary?
[00:32] Miguel: yeah sure. so the idea is prefix-first eviction, then idle-shard eviction - sorry that sounded too... uh, nested. basically we evict old prefix entries that haven't been touched within X minutes, then we escalate to full KV-compact on nodes that cross memory high watermark. thresholds we prototyped were 65%/75%/85% — it's the soft/sharp cutover. note that values are experimental.
[01:15] Jordan: and those thresholds were tuned on sequence-length 512 workloads right? not 2k?
[01:22] Miguel: right, the tuning was on our s512 sampler. we saw p99 token latency jump when we compressed too aggressively for long context sessions. so for the long sequences we suggested a higher soft threshold. there is a per-model override in the RFC.
[01:44] Ravi: question — what's the user-visible symptom of staged eviction? is it a slight latency blip or do we get 5xxs?
[01:51] Miguel: mostly latency blips, short lived recaches, sometimes increased CPU on the host. 5xxs should not happen unless eviction collides with an edge case in kernel fallback, but there is a non-zero risk. we need canary to validate.
[02:14] Maya: and does this affect KV cache warmup for dedicated pools? our dedicated customers are sensitive to cold starts.
[02:21] Lena: yes that's the tradeoff. for Dedicated we'll prefer more conservative thresholds and leverage off-peak background warmers. the private deployments can opt out or set their own policy.
[02:38] Connor: oncall perspective: if the cache thrash starts, how do we detect and classify versus normal spike? what are the ops runes?
[02:46] Ava: that's a good ops question. Lena, can you walk through alerts?
[02:50] Lena: sure — two main alerts: sustained KV memory > 80% for 3m and regen-rate > 500 keys/s for 2m. the latter correlates well with token regen. when both fire we pager to SRE and attach the evict-diagnostic bundle, plus automatic partial throttling to non-critical routes. we have example Grafana links in the doc.
[03:18] Speaker 1: link please.
[03:20] Lena: i'll post the dashboard link after this: https://redwood.internal/grafana/d/kveviction
[03:27] Jordan: ok let's pivot to rollforward vs rollback. high level thought — prefer rollforward unless model quality is catastrophically degraded. we should codify thresholds: quality regression > 2% on golden prompts or p50 cost delta > 30%? thoughts.
[03:48] Miguel: rollforward is lower impact for sessions, but it demands fast mitigations. rollback is safe for functional regressions but causes more user-facing churn. I think tie to golden set regressions and customer-visible error rate.
[04:10] Maya: also consider business owner sign-off path. if revenue-critical route, we might require explicit PM approval to rollforward.
[04:18] Ava: note: for launch we want the ability to do automated rollbacks for catastrophic perf regressions. the runbook should have both automated and manual branches.
[04:32] Ravi: can we add a short-circuit — if latency increases > 200% for two consecutive minutes on canary, auto rollback?
[04:38] Miguel: yes, that is implementable. but watch false positives - need to exclude traffic spikes. use rate-normalized metrics.
[04:51] Connor: for the canary plan, what's the traffic shape? A/B or ramp?
[04:56] Jordan: plan A: ramp 1% -> 5% -> 25% over 30m windows with steady-state 60m. Plan B: small burst sims that emulate regen waves. we run both in staging.
[05:12] Elena: who owns the canary scripting?
[05:15] Connor: I'll take it but I need the scenario definitions from Miguel.
[05:19] Miguel: sure — I'll write the scenario doc, include payload sizes, sequence lengths, and KV hit/miss expectations.
[05:27] Ava: excellent. now, runbook handoff — who writes the initial draft and who owns the oncall flow?
[05:33] Miguel: I can draft the runbook with play steps, plus a comms template for customer notice.
[05:38] Lena: SRE will own the oncall flow and alerts. I'll add call trees and escalation policy.
[05:44] Elena: product ops will maintain the stakeholder contact list and the launch-room rota.
[05:48] Ava: add that to action items.
[05:51] [short pause]
[05:55] Jordan: quick callout — we need to be explicit about latency SLOs for canary: p50/p95/p99 targets and cost tolerances. put those in the canary report.
[06:06] Miguel: agreed. initial targets: p50 < 60ms, p95 < 220ms, p99 < 420ms for s512; costs delta < 20% relative to baseline.
[06:20] Maya: note these are optimistic for long sequences but it's ok as a bar.
[06:25] Ravi: there's a question on kv-eviction ordering — do we evict globally or per-shard?
[06:31] Miguel: per-shard eviction to avoid noisy neighbor cascades. global compaction only as last resort.
[06:39] Connor: how does this interplay with our autoscaler? if evictions spike CPU, autoscaler might spin new nodes and create feedback loops.
[06:47] Lena: we can add a throttle on autoscaler triggers during an eviction window and rely on reserve capacity. that's part of the playbook.
[06:55] Ava: note: we should have a hard circuit-breaker that disables aggressive eviction if autoscaler churn > threshold. put a safety net.
[07:05] Speaker 2: a quick interjection from support - we had one ticket last week where a customer saw repeated completions fail with 502 during a background compaction. are we confident that's fixed?
[07:15] Miguel: root cause was race between compaction and kernel fallback handler. fix merged but not fully rolled to prod. need to include that fix in the canary build.
[07:25] Jordan: so action: include the compaction racefix into the canary image.
[07:30] Miguel: noted.
[07:32] Ava: let's talk communications — what do we tell customers if the launch triggers transient errors?
[07:38] Elena: we'll use the comms template. short message: "expected transient latency while caches rewarm; error rates < X% tolerated; we are monitoring". CSMs get an extended FAQ.
[07:51] Maya: also prepare a public status page blurb and internal triage doc.
[07:56] Ava: good. next: lockdown timing — freeze to codebases and deploy windows. Jordan?
[08:03] Jordan: freeze is EOD Thursday before launch; canary run Wed/Thu, rehearsal Tuesday. any hotfixes must go through expedited review and only forward rollouts.
[08:16] Ravi: are we confident on the safety margins for hardware capacity? I want a guaranteed 15% reserve.
[08:22] Lena: we can reserve burst nodes and capacity lanes. that will cost but it's part of launch budget.
[08:29] Ava: cost acceptances need PM sign-off. Jordan, add to voice.
[08:33] Jordan: on it.
[08:35] [11:00 minute mark skipped — discussion continues in detail, timestamps jump to key points]
[11:02] Connor: can we walk through an incident example? say a regen wave starts at T0, timeline to mitigation?
[11:09] Miguel: T0 detect (regen-rate alert) -> T0+2m oncall page -> T0+5m run partial throttles and enable conservative eviction -> T0+10m start canary rollback if auto-threshold hit -> T0+15m escalate to Eng L2. runbook lists exact commands and flags.
[11:30] Ava: and who's allowed to trigger an auto-rollback? SRE oncall with PM approval unless metric clearly exceeds automatic guardrail.
[11:40] Maya: add a short circuit for traffic shaping to reduce non-critical traffic by 30% while we stabilize.
[11:46] Miguel: implemented as a route-level throttle in the gateway, toggle via feature flag.
[11:50] Jordan: there's a dependency on gateway engineers to implement the flag; action for Jordan to raise with infra.
[11:57] Jordan: noted.
[12:00] [longer exchange about test instrumentation — transcription degrades slightly]
[12:28] Speaker 3: are we capturing per-request KV miss traces?
[12:31] Lena: yes, but sampling rate is low; we'll bump it for the canary.
[12:36] Miguel: don't forget to capture kernel-fallback traces too. those are crucial to debug 5xx spikes.
[12:43] Ava: ok let's close with explicit owners and dates. readbacks please.
[12:50] Miguel: I will produce the runbook draft and scenario definitions by Aug 25.
[12:55] Lena: SRE will add dashboards and alert thresholds by Aug 22 and own oncall flow.
[12:59] Connor: I'll run canaries and deliver the report by Aug 24.
[13:05] Elena: I'll schedule the rehearsal and publish the comms templates by Aug 20.
[13:12] Jordan: I'll lock the gating criteria and coordinate gateway feature flag by Aug 21.
[13:18] Ava: perfect. any other questions?
[13:21] Ravi: one more — do we need legal sign-off for the comms language?
[13:26] Elena: not usually for internal launch language but we'll run it by compliance quick.
[13:30] Ava: thanks all. we'll reconvene next Wednesday for runbook review. meeting adjourned.

Notes: there are a few places where words were unclear on the recording (speaker overlap at 12:00-12:40), please refer to posted doc for canonical definitions. Links referenced: runbook draft (to be posted), Grafana: https://redwood.internal/grafana/d/kveviction, canary scenarios doc placeholder: https://redwood.internal/docs/canary-scenarios
